findings.title: New abstract order() breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
findings.body: File common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoProvider.java line 44 adds abstract `int order()` to the public SPI without a default. Any out-of-tree implementation of CryptoProvider that compiled against the old interface will fail at runtime with AbstractMethodError and fail at compile time. The consequence is a breaking API change for custom providers. It should be a `default` method (e.g. default 0/100) to remain backwards compatible.

findings.title: Same-order providers now silently win instead of failing fast
findings.body: File common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java line 57 sorts by order and picks index 0, only logging ignored providers at debug. Previously multiple providers caused IllegalStateException. Now DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return 200, so if more than one is on the classpath the choice among them depends on ServiceLoader iteration order and is silently accepted. The consequence is non-deterministic crypto behavior and hidden misconfiguration (e.g. FIPS vs non-FIPS) that previously failed fast.

findings.title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns non-BC provider violating contract
findings.body: File authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java line 61 implements getBouncyCastleProvider() by returning `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, typically SUN/JKS, not BouncyCastle. The interface documents it as BouncyCastle provider and WildFlyElytronProvider returns null when there is no BC. Callers expecting BC/FIPS semantics that receive SUN will misbehave. It should return null like the Elytron provider when no BC is present.

findings.title: concatenatedRSToASN1DER does not validate input length
findings.body: File authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java line 103 splits `signature` into r/s with `len=signLength/2` via System.arraycopy without checking `signature.length == signLength`. A short or odd input throws raw ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of IOException, and a long input is silently truncated. The consequence is unchecked runtime exceptions and potential silent mis-signing instead of a clean invalid-signature error.

findings.title: integerToBytes silently truncates oversized/negative ECDSA integers
findings.body: File authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java line 151 in integerToBytes() strips leading bytes when `qLength < bytes.length` and pads otherwise, without checking negativity or whether stripped bytes are zero. A DER INTEGER that is negative or larger than the curve order (invalid for ECDSA) is silently truncated to the low `qLength` bytes and accepted. The consequence is acceptance of malformed signatures and incorrect raw R||S values instead of throwing IOException.

findings.title: readSequence ignores trailing bytes and indefinite length
findings.body: File authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/ASN1Decoder.java line 49 readSequence() loops while `length>0` but never verifies that exactly `length` bytes were consumed and that no trailing bytes remain, and treats indefinite length -1 as empty. A DER signature with trailing garbage after the SEQUENCE will be silently accepted by asn1derToConcatenatedRS. The consequence is lenient parsing of malformed signatures that strict DER should reject.

findings.title: Test reuses one P-256 key for ES384/ES512 and only checks round-trip
findings.body: File authz/client/src/test/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/test/ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java line 46 `test()` uses a single `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair()` (default curve, effectively P-256) for ES256, ES384 and ES512, just padding the decoded values to the larger `getSignatureLength()`. It then only asserts `rsConcat` equals `rsConcat2` after DER->raw->DER->raw, never verifying with real P-384/P-521 keys nor verifying the JWS signature. The consequence is false confidence: interop/size errors for ES384/ES512 and invalid-value handling are not exercised.
